The eyes - Of the mind, with a compleat manifestation of God's will and man's duty: both which, the works of nature, and all the writings of men discover but darkly and imperfectly.

The fear — The law and word of God, because it is both the object and the rule, and the cause of holy fear. Clean - Sincere, not adulterated with any mixture. Constant and unchangeable, the same for substance in all ages. Judgments - God's laws are frequently called his judgments, because they are the declarations of his righteous will, and as it were his judicial sentence by which he expects that men should govern themselves, and by which he will judge them at the last day.

Who — Thy law, O Lord, is holy and just and good. But I fall infinitely short of it. Cleanse - Both by justification, through the blood of thy son; and by sanctification thro' thy Holy Spirit. Though the first may seem to be principally intended, because he speaks of his past sins. Secret - From the guilt of such sins as were secret either, from others; such as none knows but God and my own conscience: or, from myself; such as I never observed, or did not discern the evil of. Pardon my unknown sins, of which I never repented particularly, as I should have done.

Presumptuous — From known and evident sins, such as are committed against knowledge, against the checks of conscience, and the motions of God's spirit. Dominion - If I be at any time tempted to such sins, Lord let them not prevail over me, and if I do fall into them, let me speedily rise again.

Let — Having prayed that God would keep him from sinful actions, he now prays that God would govern, and sanctify his words and thoughts: and this was necessary to preserve him from presumptuous sins, which have their first rise in the thoughts. Redeemer - This expression seems to be added emphatically, and with special respect to Christ, to whom alone this word Goel can properly belong. A prayer for the king, ver. 1-4. The king and the people rejoice in God, and pray for his help, ver. 5-9. To the chief musician, A psalm of David.

glossa.text: *The heavens shew forth. ((Ibid.))* First, speaking of the incarnation, he commends the preaching of the new law. ((AUG.)) The heavens, the apostles, concerning the glory of Christ in which he is equal to the Father. ((CASS.)) Or the heavens, they who sent the star. *The glory. ((Ibid.))*: That God freely forgives sins. *The works.* ((AUG.)) Those which are according to man, etc., *as far as* and these same are made night to him, giving to the darkened the knowledge which is of things human. ((CASS.)) And this so wonderfully, that it is in all tongues; and so widely, that it is in every part of the compass of the earth.

*Day unto day.* ((CASS.)) He treats of it by demonstration. ((AUG.)) *Day unto day.* The Spirit brings forth to spiritual men the fullness of wisdom, etc., *as far as* this teaching is continued by days and by nights down to those who come after.

*Speeches.* ((CASS.)) Public persuadings. *Words.* Common narrations. *Whose voices are not heard.* He would say more plainly, in whom their voices are not heard, or, the voices of all their words are heard: he does the same thing by means of the relative.

((AUG.)) The Spirit made the first men speak with all tongues, he who was to gather all nations into one; then one man was for all, so now one Christ, head and body.

*In the sun* ((CASS.)) What he praises others for having done, he himself does: he preaches the incarnation. Or in the sun, in the open sight of the world, or in labour. The sun burns, and shines, and varies the seasons. *His tabernacle.* ((AUG.)) As it were a soldier's dwelling, that is, the dispensation of his incarnation, in which he came to storm the errors of the world. Or the tabernacle, the Church in the open, not in secret, so as to lie hid. *A bridegroom.* ((CASS.)) So often promised by the prophets, a great likeness of the sacrament: therefore born of a virgin, that he might join to himself the Church a virgin. *Out of his bride-chamber.* ((AUG.)) That is, the virginal womb, where God was joined to human nature as a bridegroom to a bride. Behold, humble in mercy, but strong in majesty. *As a giant to run.* ((CASS.)) Unshaken, not to be called back, overcoming human nature by his power. *From the highest.* Here the Trinity is shewn, etc., *as far as* it marks the unity of the Trinity. *Neither is there any that can hide himself,* etc. ((AUG.)) The Word made flesh permitted no man to excuse himself out of the shadow of death: because the heat of the Word pierced even that. Or, the heat is the Spirit, whom he sent when he had returned, who is law, testimony, justice, commandment, fear and judgments, because he does these things.

*The law of the Lord.* ((CAS.)) Secondly, he praises the precepts of the New and the Old Testament. ((Ibid.)) The law given through Moses, correcting all things by the distinction of its words, and sending them on to the grace of Christ. *Converting.* ((AUG.)) By liberty, unto the imitating of himself, not pressing down with the yoke of servitude. *Souls.* Wills, not merely hands, as the Old Testament did. *The testimony.* Whatsoever *Quaecunquae* testimonies he gave to Israel are full of truth, and have given wisdom to the humble. *Wisdom:* concerning things divine.

*The justices of the Lord. ((Ibid.))* All are right in him, who taught not what he did not do, so that they who imitate them might rejoice in them, seeing they would do them freely with charity, not slavishly with fear. ((CASS.)) *Justices,* the law which justifies; whatsoever it commands is just.

*The fear of the Lord. ((Ibid.))* The fear of the world is not holy, because it is not profitable, and it changes with the times. *The fear of the Lord* is without any perturbation, because it is a love mingled with dread, because if it fears the judge, it knows him merciful. ((AUG.)) Fear, not that penal fear for earthly things, for love of which the soul is afraid, but the chaste fear whereby, the more it loves, the more it is wary of offending the bridegroom, and therefore it is not cast out, but abides. *Judgments.* The judgments of God need not another's authority.

*Desirable things. ((Ibid.))* Or, much to be desired, or much gold and stone; or much that is precious. Desirable above gold, etc., *as far as,* whose will he sets before his own, and they are sweeter than he himself is to himself. *Above gold,* that is, everything that is sought after, whether for riches, or for power, or for pleasure. *Honey.* The food of God is honey; that is, one now loosed from the world; and the honeycomb, that is, because he is still wrapped about, for whom there is need of the pressure of God's hand squeezing him out, that he may go into life.

*Who understandeth sins. ((Ibid.))* Thirdly he asks to be purged of vices, that he may be a worthy psalmist, to report these sacraments. To a mind that sees, truth is sweet, and judgments sweet; to one that does not see, what sweetness is there? But why is it not seen? Because of sins: nor is it any wonder: *For who understandeth sins?* ((CASS.)) *Sins:* all of them, for certain of them are known. *Mine* defile, *others'* afflict, and now spare, drive back the persuader. *From my secret ones.* He includes all sins under two heads, etc., *as far as* whereby man was seduced; and by consenting he made it his own. ((AUG.)) There is no greater sin than to apostatize from God, which is the beginning of pride: but pride is the beginning and the cause of all sin.

notes.text: Sprinkle — "This signifies both the blood of Christ sprinkled upon their conscience, to take away their guilt, as the water of purification was sprinkled, to take away their ceremonial uncleanness and the grace of the spirit sprinkled on the whole soul, to purify it from all corrupt inclinations and dispositions."

A new heart — A new frame of soul, a mind changed, from sinful to holy, from carnal to spiritual. A heart in which the law of God is written, Jer. xxxi, 33. A sanctified heart, in which the almighty grace of God is victorious, and turns it from all sin to God. A new spirit - A new, holy frame in the spirit of man; which is given to him, not wrought by his own power. The stony - The senseless unfeeling. Out of your flesh - Out of you. Of flesh - That is, quite of another temper, hearkening to God's law, trembling at his threats, molded into a compliance with his whole will; to forbear, do, be, or suffer what God will, receiving the impress of God, as soft wax receives the impress of the seal.

My spirit — The Holy Spirit of God, which is given to, and dwelleth in all true believers. And cause you - Sweetly, powerfully, yet without compulsion; for our spirits, framed by God's spirit to a disposition suitable to his holiness, readily concurs. Ye shall keep - Be willing; and able to keep the judgments, and to walk in the statutes of God, which is, to live in all holiness.
Ye shall dwell — Observe: then, and not before, are these promises to be fulfilled to the house of Israel. And I will be your God - This is the foundation of the top-stone of a believer's happiness.
Panteth — After the enjoyment of thee in thy sanctuary.
Thirsteth — Not after vain useless idols, but after the only true and living God. Appear - In the place of his special presence and publick worship.

Remember — My banishment from God's presence, and mine enemies triumphs. In me - I breathe out my sorrows and complaints to God within my own breast. The multitudes - Israelites, who went thither in great numbers. Holy-day - Or that kept the feast, the three solemn festival solemnities, which they kept holy unto the Lord.

For — Hebrew. for the salvations of his face, for those supports, deliverances and comforts which I doubt not I shall enjoy both in his presence and sanctuary, and from his presence, and the light of his countenance.

Therefore — Therefore that I may revive my drooping spirits. Remember - I will consider thy infinite mercy and power, and faithfulness. Mizar - From all the parts of the land, to which I shall be driven; whether from the parts beyond Jordan on the east: or mount Hermon, which was in the northern parts.

Deep — One affliction comes immediately after another, as if it were called for by the former. A metaphor taken from violent and successive showers of rain; which frequently come down from heaven, as it were at the noise, or call of God's water spouts.
Command — Will effectually confer upon me. Loving-kindness - His blessings, the effects of his loving-kindness.
As — As a sword, which cutteth the very bones, so painful are their reproaches. The psalmist appeals to God, ver. 1, 2. Prays to be restored to the public ordinances, and trusts in God, ver. 3-5.

glossa.text:
*As the hart desireth,* etc. ((AUG.)) This voice suits catechumens, and also all who are still journeying abroad.

*The hart.* The hart, burdened with age, its hairs and horns growing out, draws in a serpent by its nostrils: whence, burning with the venom, it most ardently desires a fountain from which to drink; and when it has drunk, it lays aside its horns and its hairs.

*It hath thirsted.* ((AUG.)) He determines his desire, because the hart could be understood to desire a fountain for the sake of drinking, or of washing; here all desire is shown to be toward God. *When shall I come.* What is quicker to God is slow to the desire of man. Such a hart, while it runs, suffers those who insult; whence: *My tears have been my bread.* In prosperity also, which he despises, as in adversity. *Bread.* ((CASS.)) Not bitterness, or destruction, but *bread.*

*These things I remembered.* ((AUG.)) While they ask, Where is thy God? I also have meditated through all these visible things, and through my own soul, that through those outward things I may find the invisible things of God. Behold the understanding of the title. *I poured out. ((Ibid.))* For understanding and attaining I have spread it out above itself. *I poured out.* ((CASS.)) Or, I have rejoiced. My soul is melted within me; not outside, but pricked with compunction it returns into itself. Although I do not see God visibly, yet I consider that through the Church, in which the saints are wonderful, I shall come to the heavenly Jerusalem, taken captive by the sweetness of the angelic praise, which is received by the mind. *Into the place of the tabernacle.* ((AUG.)) The tabernacle of God on earth, etc., *as far as,* that is, of those rejoicing in the eternal refreshment. *In the voice of exultation. ((Ibid.))* Of the eternal festival there sounds something sweet to the heart: whence the hart is snatched away to the fountains of waters, and is soothed. But because the world makes a din, and the flesh weighs down the soul, comparing this sorrow with those joyful things, he says:

*Why art thou sad?* etc. ((CASS.)) Of the disturbances against which reason strengthens the sensual soul with hope of God. *Why dost thou trouble?* ((AUG.)) Who, if thou searchest, there is nothing in the world for which thou shouldst owe this: hope rather for the saving remedy still, and if not now, fully in time to come. *Hope.* ((CASS.)) Or he can hope, because *still* in the present *I will confess,* that is, I will do penance for my sins, that I may not withstand thee.

*To myself.* Turned to God he tells the troublings from himself, the end of them from God: whence in him is his hope. And this is *to myself,* or from myself. ((CASS.)) Behold, he who above was correcting the soul to the condition of man, having turned back says here that the soul is troubled by itself, which, were there not the vices of the flesh, would remain tranquil. Behold out of what diversity man is composed. As if: therefore, that is, on account of the troublings of the soul, *I will be mindful.* ((AUG.)) That is, I hasten to thee, because thou shuttest out all evils. Behold the remedy by which he may escape the troublings: whence he subjoins for what things he is mindful: *Of the land of Jordan,* where the Lord consecrated baptism, in which the humbled are washed, and become fruitful earth. ((CASS.)) He who is mindful of these things is not troubled by evils. *Therefore mindful.* ((AUG.)) Whereby the soul is troubled toward me, therefore *mindful,* etc. No one runs to remission, save he who is displeasing to himself, save he who confesses himself a sinner: which *Hermoniim* denotes; no one confesses unless he humbles himself, which is denoted in *the little one. Jordan. ((Ibid.))* A going down. Descend therefore that thou mayest be lifted up. ((CASS.)) In the Jordan the Lord consecrated baptism, in which the humbled are washed, and become fruitful earth, which yields fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold ((Matth. XIII)). *Hermoniim.* ((AUG.)) A small mountain beside the Jordan, etc., *as far as* because it is not among the proud, but among the humble, that one is mindful of God.

*Deep unto deep. ((Ibid.))* It is fitting that I be mindful, etc., *as far as* and on account of all these things I pray in adversities, and this is: *With me a prayer. ((Ibid.))* Or *deep calleth unto deep,* that is, the judgment which God brought upon the sinner, etc., *as far as* because he fears the judgments. *Of the cataracts.* Cataracts, according to the letter, are the mouths of rivers.
*In the day. ((Ibid.))* That is, in prosperity, etc., *as far as* whence we may live in adversity. *With me a prayer. ((Ibid.))* Prayer in troublings is mine, and this is with me.
*Why hast thou forgotten.* ((CASS.)) Why dost thou now suffer me to be vexed with these miseries? He saw what sweetness of the fatherland there was, and shuddered at the perils of the world.

*While my bones are broken.* ((AUG.)) As it were bones are broken, while the strength of patience is afflicted, at which the wicked laugh. This is that reproach: *While it is said to me: Where is he?* either there is none, or he cares not for thee.

notes.text:
And set me down — So it seemed to me in the vision. Which is a lively representation of a threefold resurrection:

1. Of the resurrection of souls, from the death of sin, to the life of righteousness:

2. The resurrection of the church from an afflicted state, to liberty and peace:

3. The resurrection of the body at the great day, especially the bodies of believers to life eternal.
And he — The Lord.

Prophesied — Declared these promises. As I prophesied - While I was prophesying. A noise - A rattling of the bones in their motion. A shaking - A trembling or commotion among the bones, enough to manifest a divine presence, working among them. Came together - Glided nearer and nearer, 'till each bone met the bone to which it was to be joined. Of all the bones of all those numerous slain, not one was missing, not one missed its way, not one missed its place, but each knew and found its fellow. Thus in the resurrection of the dead, the scattered atoms shall be arranged in their proper place and order, and every bone come to his bone, by the same wisdom and power by which they were first formed in the womb of her that is with child.
Came up — Gradually spreading itself.
Prophesy — Declare what my will is. O breath - The soul, whose emblem here is wind; which, as it gently blew upon these lifeless creatures, each was inspired with its own soul or spirit.
And the breath — The spirit of life, or the soul, Gen. ii, 7.
The whole house — The emblem of the house of Israel. Are dried - Our state is as hopeless, as far from recovery, as dried bones are from life.
I will open — Though your captivity be as death, your persons close as the grave, yet I will open those graves.
Justified — Upon terms of strict justice.

For — This is not a reason of what he last said, but an argument to enforce his petition delivered, ver. 1. Soul - My life; nothing less will satisfy him. Dead - I am in as hopeless a condition in the eye of man, as those that have lain long in the grave.
The days — What thou hast done for thy servants in former times.
As land — Thirsteth for rain.

Morning — Seasonably and speedily. David blesses God for his mercies, ver. 1-4. Prays against his enemies, ver. 5-8. Promises to praise him, ver.9-11. The happiness of those who serve God, ver. 12-15. A psalm of David.

glossa.text: *O Lord, hear,* etc. ((CAS.)) First he takes his exordium; secondly he narrates his own evils, and what he has done against them, there, *because he has persecuted;* thirdly the supplication is set down, confirmed by reasons, there, *hear speedily;* fourthly the joyful conclusion is set down, there, *thy spirit.* He admonishes to penance, and to prayer, that we should pray. In the person of the whole Christ he says: *O Lord,* etc. *In thy truth.* ((CAS.)) This is not against the humility which was asking to be heard: but it is the truth and justice of God, that he should not dispute with the one asking, that he should not judge him who condemns himself; whence it is added: *and enter not,* he did not ask for the justice of judgment. ((AUG., CAS.)) *In thy truth, in thy justice.* Or he calls justice and truth that which spares the penitent, and absolves those who condemn themselves, and he takes *truth and justice* for the same thing. And the sense is, *in thy truth, and thy justice,* that is, according to the justice and truth which thou grantest to the penitent and to those who accuse themselves.

*And enter not into judgment.* ((AUG.)) They enter into judgment with the Lord who establish their own justice, which this humble man does not do; whence the prophet: *Why will you contend with me in judgment? You have all forsaken me, says the Lord. With thy servant.* It is unworthy to contend with a servant, not to say with a friend: and if thou sayest 'friend', and I 'servant', a fugitive I return, I seek peace, *I am not worthy to be called thy son.*
*Because he has persecuted.* ((CAS.)) The second part, where there is the narration of the evils which he suffers, and what he has done against them.

*I have been mindful.* ((AUG.)) This the members say, etc., *as far as* but thou hast begun not to be. *I have meditated.* Because assuredly all things are good, wherein he perceives that whatsoever of good is in him, is from God. *In the works of the hands.* As if he should say: I have sought the craftsman in the work, and in all created things the creator: thy creature has been made a spectacle for me.

*I have been mindful of the days.* ((CAS.)) This man, calling to mind that he made heaven and earth, and that he did good to the ancients, forgets the miseries of the world. And out of those things which God has made he consoles himself.

*Speedily.* ((CAS.)) The third part, where the supplication confirmed by reasons is set down. *The spirit hath failed.* ((AUG.)) Let thy Spirit fill me, because mine has failed: already I am poor in spirit. For in whom his own spirit lives, he is proud in his own spirit, and is lifted up against God. Whence elsewhere: *Thou shalt take away their spirits, and they shall fail ((Psal. CIII))*. *Into the pit.* He goes down into the deep who loses even confession, as one who sets before himself licence to sin without hope of pardon, the reins of iniquity let loose. Such a man does not hear God saying: *Turn to me, and I will turn to you ((Zach. I))*.

*In the morning.* ((CAS.)) After the night of sins. ((AUG.)) It is morning, when sins are loosed. *Make the way known to me.* This God has done, etc., *as far as* we shall come to the pure light, to the Word in the beginning with God. *The soul.* (CAS.) As a vessel I have brought it to the fountain: fill it therefore.

*Thy good spirit.* ((CAS.)) The fourth part, where the joyful conclusion is. *For thy name's sake, O Lord, thou wilt quicken me in thy equity.* The grace of God is here commended: because he says that he is quickened not out of merits, but out of the name, which is Jesus; yet along with this the grace of equity shows mercy, because although God does all things freely, it belongs nevertheless to his justice to justify the suppliants whom he sees the demons assail.

notes.text: Taken away — Abolished, and put an end to the judgments thy sins brought upon thee. Thine enemy - The Babylonian. Is in the midst - He is returned to redeem and govern thee. Any more - While thy carriage is as becomes my presence with thee, thou shalt neither fear, nor feel the like evils.
Sorrowful — That mourn their distance from the solemn worship of God. Who are of thee - Thy children. Reproach - The taunts of their enemies.
Undo — I will break their power and dissolve their kingdom. That halteth - Who is in trouble and ready to fall. Driven out - Into remote countries.
A praise — So the universal church of the first-born will be, in the great day. And then the Israel of God be made a name and a praise to all eternity.

Salvation — The redemption of the world by the Messiah: which was hitherto reserved was a secret among the Jews, yea was not throughly known by the most of the Jews themselves. Righteousness - His faithfulness in accomplishing this great promise. Israel is required to praise God, for their hasty constitution both in church and state, ver. 1-5. Some instances of the happy administration of it, ver. 6-9.

glossa.text:
*Sing ye to the Lord.* ((CASS.)) First he speaks of the showing forth of the saving right hand.

*He hath saved.* ((AUG.)) It is a greater thing that he raised up the whole world from eternal death, than that he raised the dead. *To himself.* Many are saved bodily, but to themselves, not to him: they who, having received bodily health, grow wanton, but they who by faith are healed within, are healed to him, or save themselves.

*Salvation . . . justice.* ((AUG.)) He who saves and justifies. *He hath revealed.* Things to come were foretold under a veil by the prophets: but the veil has been taken away, since *truth is sprung out of the earth.*

*Of mercy and of truth.* ((AUG.)) *Mercy* is that whereby he promised, *truth* follows upon this, because he rendered it. But to whom? *To Israel,* that is, to him who now by faith sees the truth, afterwards by sight.
*All.* ((ID.)) Because Christ was not given to certain men only.
*Rejoice ye.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he says that in all ways he is to be praised and declared, because the judge is come.

*With ductile trumpets and with the voice of a trumpet of horn.* ((AUG.)) Of brass, which are drawn out by beating, etc., *as far as* as the horn cleaves to the flesh, and surpasses it. ((HIERON.)) With ductile trumpets, of silver, after the manner of the Jews. Mystically, drawn out under the hammer of the whole earth, that is, the devil. ((AUG.)) Tribulation is the beating; advancement, the drawing out: such a trumpet was Job, whence he sounded as a trumpet, saying: *The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away.*

*Let it be moved.* ((ID.)) That is, let the sea of the law be made sweet, the wood of the cross being set therein. *And the fulness thereof.* All the sacraments of the law, etc., *as far as* but *the rivers,* etc. *The earth.* ((CASS.)) That is, every sinner.

*The world of the earth.* All earthly men. *In justice.* ((AUG.)) Because they did not merit mercy. *The peoples.* ((CASS.)) The faithful out of the Jews and the Gentiles, who shall receive things equal to their merits.

notes.text: As many as have been baptized into Jesus Christ have been baptized into his death — In baptism we, through faith, are ingrafted into Christ; and we draw new spiritual life from this new root, through his Spirit, who fashions us like unto him, and particularly with regard to his death and resurrection.

We are buried with him — Alluding to the ancient manner of baptizing by immersion. That as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory - Glorious power. Of the Father, so we also, by the same power, should rise again; and as he lives a new life in heaven, so we should walk in newness of life. This, says the apostle, our very baptism represents to us.
For — Surely these two must go together; so that if we are indeed made conformable to his death, we shall also know the power of his resurrection.

Our old man — Coeval with our being, and as old as the fall; our evil nature; a strong and beautiful expression for that entire depravity and corruption which by nature spreads itself over the whole man, leaving no part uninfected. This in a believer is crucified with Christ, mortified, gradually killed, by virtue of our union with him. That the body of sin - All evil tempers, words, and actions, which are the "members" of the "old man," Colossians iii, 5, might be destroyed.
For he that is dead — With Christ. Is freed from the guilt of past, and from the power of present, sin, as dead men from the commands of their former masters.
Dead with Christ — Conformed to his death, by dying to sin.
He died to sin — To atone for and abolish it. He liveth unto God - A glorious eternal life, such as we shall live also.

glossa.text: *Know you not.* Being dead to sin, which is done in baptism, we ought not to live to it again, so that it should be necessary to die to it again: because in the death of Christ, that is, in the likeness of the death of Christ, that as he died once in the flesh and lives always, so we, having died once to evil through baptism, may always live to good. Or he says *in the death:* because death is the cause of this purification.

*Buried together.* Whatever was done in the cross of Christ, in the burial, in the resurrection, in the ascension, in the sitting at the right hand, was so done that the Christian life might be conformed to these things, which were mystically not only spoken but also done. Consider the several things of Christ, in whom the old man had lived according to punishment, hunger, thirst and the like, not according to fault: in this manner he ended and disposed the oldness, so that, enduring the pain of the cross, he had his limbs thus stretched out and fastened, that they might not be moved to their former acts, from which, buried also, he rested, withdrawn from human sight, requiring of us that we lay aside the oldness of sins with the sorrow and groaning of penance: that our limbs be fastened together through continence and justice, lest we return to our former evils, from which we should so perfectly rest that neither the sight nor the memory of them be had: and not only does he require this of us in the sacrament of the passion, but he also brings it about, if we will to imitate him. *He rose again from the dead.* The death and the resurrection of Christ are also sacraments.

*The old man.* That is, the old acts are crucified, that is, dead. Our oldness and our curse consist in two things, namely in fault and in punishment. But Christ by his single oldness consumed our twofold one. For in the sepulchre he rested one day and two nights. By the one day his single oldness is signified, but by the two nights our twofold one; whence: Christ blotted out our fault, present, past, and future. The past by forgiving it, the present by drawing us back from it, the future by conferring grace that we might avoid it. The punishment likewise he consumed, wholly blotting out the punishment of Gehenna, so that they who truly repent may not feel it. The temporal punishment, however, he did not entirely take away: for hunger, thirst, death and the like remain; but he cast down its reign and dominion, and at the last he will utterly destroy it.

*Knowing that Christ. (AUG)*. One rose again now not to die. Lazarus rose again, but to die; the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue rose again, but to die; the son of the widow rose again, but to die: Christ rose again not to die. Hear the Apostle, *Christ rising again,* etc. Hope for such a resurrection, and for the sake of this be a Christian, not for the sake of the happiness of this earth.

*For in that he died to sin. ((AUG.))* The Apostle commends the sacrament of baptism, that as he, by dying once, is preached as having died by a likeness of sin, so whoever has been baptized in him may die to that same thing of which that was the likeness, that is, to sin; and may live by being born again from the font, as he lived by rising again from the sepulchre.
*So do you also.* Whatever he said above belongs to men through the grace of Christ, here he attributes to the Romans.

notes.text: Judah — Or Israel, one tribe being put for all. Judah he mentions as the chief of all the tribes.
The mountains — Horeb and Sinai, two tops of one mountain, and other neighbouring mountains.

Tremble — The mountains did more than what was fit at the appearance of the great God. We are to give glory to God, not to ourselves or idols, ver. 1-8. By trusting in his promise and blessing, ver. 9-15. And by praising him, ver. 16-18.

glossa.text:
*At the going out.* ((AUG.)) Here things past are not related, but things to come are foretold, because in those deeds things to come were signified: and therefore not all the things which were done there are spoken of here, but certain of them otherwise, lest he be thought to be recounting things past. ((CASS.)) First the Prophet tells what wonders God gave to the Hebrews in figure, and to Christians in spirit. Secondly he asks why these things were done, there, *What ailed thee, O sea?* Thirdly he reproves the empty idols of the Gentiles, and commends the religion of God, there, *the idols of the Gentiles.*

*At the going out.* As it were, when Israel, that is, the house of Jacob, went out of Egypt, that is, from a barbarous people.

 *Barbarous.* ((AUG.)) That tongue is barbarous which praises not God.
*It was made.* ((CASS.)) As that people, when it went out of Egypt, etc., *as far as* they are able to resist vices, and this.

*The sea saw,* that is, the sinners of the world. *Jordan,* they who by divers desires snatch men into the great sea, that is, into the embittering malice of this world; but these things cease at the coming of the Lord, being as it were turned backward.

*The sea saw.* ((AUG.)) This is here said otherwise than it was done. There it is read to have stood on that side from which the waters were flowing down, nor is anything said there of the mountains skipping; but both the things done there and the things said here are figures.

*Rams.* ((ID.)) Who with the horns of both, etc., *as far as* every knowledge lifting itself up against Christ. *The hills.* ((CASS.)) From tilling, the middling sort: for these things are not according to the letter; whence also by the sea and by Jordan, that is, by the ancient deeds, doubt not that those things are signified which today are done spiritually.
*What ailed thee.* ((ID.)) Secondly he asks why these things were, that he may stir up wonder. And he resolves it: *At the face of the Lord.*

*At the face.* ((ID.)) One answer for two, because one author both made the ages to be astonished, and made his own, that is, the mountains and the hills, to rejoice: for at the appearing of Christ men were moved from their own superstition to the worship of God.

*At the face of the God of Jacob.* And as though one should ask, who is the Lord? The God of Jacob, not a new one; who makes them wrestle.

*Who turned the rock.* ((ID.)) The hard hearts of the Jews, unto the water of baptism.

*The crag.* The Gentiles, that they also may pour forth the watering fountains of preaching.

((AUG.)) That is, himself, hard before, while he was not known, etc., *as far as* he might overflow upon all that believe, saying: *If any man thirst, let him come to me and drink.*
*The house of Israel.* ((CASS.)) Here he shows the profit of the Christian religion.
*The house of Aaron.* ((AUG.)) But lest that should seem to be already a thing possessed by the greater which to the lesser is a hope, he adds, *The house of Aaron.*
*Mindful.* ((CASS.)) That he might convert them, and he blessed the converted through the same.

*Upon you.* ((AUG.)) Because the number of teachers increased.

*Upon the children.* Because the number of followers also increased. Therefore ye both, fathers and sons, are blessed of the Lord, who made you *heaven* in the greater, *and earth* in the lesser; or who made every creature.

*Blessed be ye of the Lord.* ((CASS.)) He who above wished to be blessed, now with confidence says, *Blessed,* which belongs to God, that ye may serve him. Truly *of the Lord,* because even *the heaven of heaven,* that is, Christ, is unto the honour of the Lord; or,

*The heaven of heaven,* that is, the empyrean, he gave to the Lord Christ, according as he is man. *But the earth.* This lower earth he gave. *To the children of men.* That in it they may purify themselves; or the people to the preachers; whence: As the Father hath sent me, and I will send you ((Joan. VI)).

*The heaven of heaven.* ((AUG.)) He speaks of those whose minds, etc., *as far as* whom the weak cannot yet see without a support.
*Nor all they that go down.* ((CASS.)) Or, not all they that go down; because the saints also went down, but not into the lower place.

notes.text: Mark xvi, 1; Luke xxiv, 1; John xx, 1

An angel of the Lord had rolled away the stone and sat upon it — St. Luke and St. John speak of two angels that appeared: but it seems as if only one of them had appeared sitting on the stone without the sepulchre, and then going into it, was seen with another angel, sitting, one where the head, the other where the feet of the body had lain.

Come, see the place where the Lord lay — Probably in speaking he rose up, and going before the women into the sepulchre, said, Come, see the place. This clearly reconciles what St. John relates, John xx, 12, this being one of the two angels there mentioned.

There shall ye see him — In his solemn appearance to them all together. But their gracious Lord would not be absent so long: he appeared to them several times before then. Lo, I have told you - A solemn confirmation of what he had said.
Hail — The word in its primary sense means, "Rejoice:" in its secondary and more usual meaning, "Happiness attend you."
Go tell my brethren -- I still own them as such, though they so lately disowned and forsook me.

glossa.text: *In the evening,* etc. ((HIER.)) That the different times of these women, etc., *as far as* they could not approach, they approach in the morning. *Mary Magdalen, and the other Mary.* Two women of one name and of one devotion signify two peoples embracing with equal devotion the passion and the resurrection of Christ.

*An earthquake.* As in the passion, so also in the resurrection there is a movement of the earth: and it signifies that the hearts of earthly men are to be moved to penance through faith in the passion and the resurrection. *He rolled back the stone.* He could go out from the sepulchre while it was closed, who was born from the virgin's womb while it was closed. The rolling back of the stone signifies the unlocking of the sacraments of Christ, which were covered by the veil of the letter: which being taken away, the resurrection, the abolition of death, life eternal began to be preached throughout the whole world.
*As lightning.* In the whiteness of the garment he signified that he would be gentle to the just, in the terror of the lightning he signifies that he will be terrible to the reprobate.
*Fear not.* You who see your own fellow citizens. Let those fear who do not belong to their fellowship.
*And going quickly.* Nor is it granted to us to keep this joy in the secret of the heart, but to lay it open to those who love in like manner.

*With fear and joy.* The affection in them is twofold, of fear and of joy. The one from the greatness of the miracle, the other from desire of him who was rising again, and each urged on the womanly step.

*And behold Jesus,* etc. So Christ meets with his help all who begin the way of the virtues. *And they held.* It was said above that he went out while the monument was closed, that thou mightest understand the body to be immortal: here his feet are held, that thou mightest prove the flesh to be true. And because they trembled at so great a vision, fear is first driven out: *Fear not,* that with a peaceful mind they might be able to hear the things that are said. These women hold his feet, who adore him raised up again: but she who did not yet know that the Son of God had risen again deservedly hears: *Touch me not, for I am not yet ascended to my Father ((Joan XX))*.

*Tell.* As a woman told the death-bearing words of the serpent, so now the words of the life-giver, that from her from whom death then came, now life may come. *To my brethren.* Before he called them servants also, now brethren, that he may teach that after the resurrection he has taken up again the same humanity, and that they may hope for the same.

echoes.text: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”
echoes.note: To Cain: sin 'is crouching at the door; its desire is for you, but you must rule over it.' Paul's 'do not let sin reign (basileueto) in your mortal body' (6:12) personifies Sin as a power seeking to master a person who must instead exercise dominion over it. The shared image of Sin as an external would-be ruler the believer must refuse to obey is striking; many read 6:12 against this primal scene.

echoes.text: Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:
echoes.note: Redemption-from-bondage language: God brings Israel 'out from under the burdens' and 'redeems' them from slavery. Romans 6:6 ('no longer in bondage to sin', douleuein) and 6:7 ('freed from sin') run the exodus slavery/liberation pattern onto sin as the new Pharaoh. The slavery-redemption typology is strong thematically though the verbal contact here is diffuse; the fuller slavery exposition comes in 6:15-23.

echoes.text: The hand of Yahweh was on me, and he brought me out in the Spirit of Yahweh, and set me down in the midst of the valley; and it was full of bones. He caused me to pass by them all around: and behold, there were very many in the open valley; and behold, they were very dry. He said to me, Son of man, can these bones live? I answered, Lord Yahweh, you know. Again he said to me, Prophesy over these bones, and tell them, you dry bones, hear Yahweh’s word. Thus […]
echoes.note: The valley of dry bones: God brings the dead up from their graves to new life by his Spirit. Paul's death-and-burial-then-'newness of life' (6:4) and 'alive from the dead' (6:13) share the figural movement of resurrection-as-new-existence, though Paul grounds it christologically rather than nationally.

echoes.text: I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: New heart and new spirit enabling obedience; 'newness of life' (6:4, kainotes zoes) coheres with the prophetic promise of interior renewal. Faint and disputed verbal contact, but the renewal/new-walk theme is shared.

echoes.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
echoes.note: 'After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.' A type of death-and-resurrection-to-life that early Christian reading connected to Christ's raising; resonates with 6:4-5,8-9 union in death and resurrection. Faint and contested.

echoes.text: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
echoes.note: The angel's appearance 'like lightning' and clothing 'white as snow' echoes Daniel's vision of the man clothed in linen whose 'face was like the appearance of lightning' and whose body shone. Matthew draws on the standard Danielic theophany-angelophany vocabulary to mark this messenger as a heavenly being.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
echoes.note: 'His clothing white as snow' matches the Ancient of Days whose 'clothing was white as snow.' The dazzling-white garment is a marker of divine/heavenly glory; Matthew transfers the apocalyptic radiance to the resurrection messenger.

echoes.text: Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
echoes.note: 'A great earthquake' (seismos) recalls the theophany at Sinai where the whole mountain quaked greatly at the LORD's descent. Matthew uses earthquake as a recurring sign of divine intervention (cf. 27:51), framing the resurrection as a world-shaking act of God.

echoes.text: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
echoes.note: The eschatological awakening of those who 'sleep in the dust' to everlasting life stands behind the resurrection scene; the guards becoming 'like dead men' while the dead one rises figurally inverts Daniel's resurrection hope.

echoes.text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
echoes.note: 'Don't be afraid' (me phobeisthe) on the angel's lips is the recurrent assurance-of-presence formula God speaks to his people: 'Fear not, for I am with you.' It frames the empty tomb as a moment of divine reassurance, anticipating 28:20.

echoes.text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid, neither be dismayed: for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”
echoes.note: The 'do not be afraid... for the LORD your God is with you' charge before entering the land resonates with the angel's reassurance and the disciples' coming commission; a faint commissioning-courage motif.

echoes.text: He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood opposite him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,
echoes.note: The women's prostration and grasping Jesus' feet in worship recalls the patriarchal pattern of falling before a divine visitor; a faint thematic resonance with theophanic reverence rather than a verbal borrowing.

echoes.text: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him. I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him. The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?” I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him […]
echoes.note: The women seeking at dawn, then finding and taking hold of the beloved ('I held him and would not let him go') has long been read figurally alongside the women grasping Jesus' feet; a contested, allusive resonance in early reception.

echoes.text: I will declare your name to my brothers. In the midst of the assembly, I will praise you.
echoes.note: Jesus' instruction to tell 'my brothers' echoes the vindicated sufferer who declares God's name 'to my brothers' after deliverance; given Matthew's heavy use of Psalm 22 at the cross (27:35,43,46), the brother-language here may extend that figural arc.

lines: We have come while it is still dark, with one small flame between us — the way God's first word split the night and called up the light.
Christ is our light.
This is the fire that went before them in the wilderness, the dawn that found the sea rolled back and the people walking through on dry ground.
Christ is our light.

Christ is our light.

Christ is our light. Christ is risen, alleluia!
